union of shabad and baani items.

isPublic.description:
Whether the folder is publicly shareable via its link. Client-controlled
(rides the sync PUT). Only mypothi folders may be public. Defaults to false.

pinned.description:
Whether the folder is pinned to the top of the list. Client-controlled
(rides the sync PUT). Defaults to false.

folders.description: All live folders for this user, across every source

deletedFolderIds.description:
Ids of folders deleted server-side — by this or another device — since
the `since` the caller sent (every tombstone when `since` is absent).
The device removes them locally and retires its own tombstones for them.

rejectedFolderIds.description:
On a PUT: ids in the request that were NOT applied because the server
already held a newer version (written by another device). The device
should adopt the returned copy for those. Empty on a GET.

syncedAt.description:
Server watermark covering every clock in this response (ms since epoch).
Send it back as `since` on the next GET to receive only what changed.

updatedAt.description: Server-set last-write timestamp (ISO 8601), for "last synced" UI

source.description:
Scope of the replacement — only folders of this source are replaced;
folders of other sources are left untouched.

folders.description:
Full replacement set of the user's folders for `source`.
Every folder MUST have `folder.source === source`.

name.description: Name for the saved copy. Defaults to the shared folder's name.

avatar.description:
Profile picture as a data URL (`data:<mime>;base64,...`), or null when the
user has not uploaded one.

avatarUpdatedAt.description: When the avatar was last set (ISO 8601), or null.

name.description: Display name on record (may be null — the web app keeps its own override)

shabadId.description: Shabad identifier to favorite. Provide exactly one of shabadId / baniId.

baniId.description:
Bani identifier to favorite (a whole bani, e.g. Sundar Gutka). Provide
exactly one of shabadId / baniId.

verseId.description: Optional verse to highlight within the shabad

comment.description: Optional free-text note about the favorite

date.description:
The DEVICE'S LOCAL calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Not a timestamp, deliberately. A timestamp would have to be bucketed into a
day server-side, and the only day the server can derive is the UTC one —
which puts most Indian morning nitnem (Amrit Vela is 21:30–00:30 UTC the
day before) under the wrong date. The device already knows which day it
was; it just has to say so.

readingSeconds.description: Total seconds READ on this device on this day. Cumulative, not a delta.

listeningSeconds.description: Total seconds LISTENED on this device on this day.

deviceId.description:
Which device these rows belong to. Part of the key, not merely metadata:
a device owns its own row for a date, so two devices on the same day are
summed rather than one overwriting the other.

days.description:
The days this device has changed since it last synced — normally one.

Capped so a corrupt or hostile client cannot make one request rewrite an
account's entire history; 400 days covers a year of backfill with room to
spare.

version.description: App/schema version that produced this snapshot

capturedAt.description:
When the snapshot was captured client-side (ISO-8601). Its calendar day is
the idempotency key — same-day re-syncs upsert (last-write-wins).

deviceId.description:
Which device produced this snapshot. No longer the sync identity — the row
is keyed on the account from the bearer token. Still required, because it
is how snapshots pushed before the user had an account are adopted on their
first authenticated sync.

userId.description:
IGNORED. The owning account is resolved from the bearer token and never
from the body — a request must not be able to nominate whose data it
writes.

Kept only because the shipped app still sends `userId: null` and `main.ts`
sets `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so removing it would 400 every existing
client. Delete once the app has stopped sending it.

payload.description:

`streaks.current/longest` and `totals.banisCompleted/daysActive` are read
out into indexed columns.

Present and `true` when a snapshot already existed for the day and was
upserted with this one (HTTP 200 instead of 201).

members.description:
A few of the people reading this path, for the card's avatar stack.

A PREVIEW, not the list — capped at three, because that is what the card
draws. `memberCount` carries the real total, so "by 5 readers" stays true
with three faces shown. Empty on a personal path.

Sent here rather than fetched per path: the home screen already makes this
one call, and asking `GET /members` once per card would turn a single
request into one per path.

relationship.description:
How the caller reaches it. `OWNER` also covers a path they created and
later shared — they are both owner and admin, and it appears once.

Null for a path they joined — they have no local copy to match it against.

memberCount.description:
How many active members the path has, counting the ones not previewed.
Zero on a personal path.

role.description: What the caller may do in this path.

id.description:
The internal path id. Every group route is keyed on this, never on the
legacy per-account `pathId`.

angNumber.description: The ang the group has read to.

verseId.description: The verse the group has read to.

memberCount.description: Active members only. Requested and removed people are not counted.

stateVersion.description:
Bumped by every group change, so a client can cache the plan and refetch
only when something actually moved.

status.description:
Members are active until they leave or are removed. There is no
`INVITED` state because a valid link joins the path directly.

readingDays.description:
How many days this member has taken part in the reading.

Present only on the members list, which is the one place it is worth the
count. Earned by reading a turn, or by following one for long enough that
it counts as taking part rather than glancing at the screen.

hasAvatar.description:
Whether this member has a picture to fetch.

The image itself is NOT inlined. A group list is read far more often than
the pictures change, and a handful of base64 avatars would dominate every
response — so the list stays light and the client fetches what it needs
from `GET /paths/:id/members/:memberId/avatar`, where HTTP caching does
the work.

avatarUpdatedAt.description:
When that picture last changed, or null when there is none.

The client appends it to the avatar URL so a changed picture busts its own
cache, and an unchanged one is never refetched.

id.description:
Membership id. Slots and sessions reference this, not a user id, so
history survives the account being deleted.

userId.description: The person, when they still have an account. Null once they delete it.

isMine.description:
True when this membership is the caller's own.

`userId` alone cannot answer that on the client: the app knows its email,
never its user id. Without this a device could not tell its own membership
from anybody else's — so a reader who already held the turn was shown as
somebody else reading, and offered to "follow" themselves.

displayLabel.description: What history shows when there is no user row left to name.

dates.description: Participation timestamps. Clients format these in the reader’s local timezone to determine calendar days.

role.description:
Granting admin is how the group is handed on. Removing the last admin is
refused while other members remain.

token.description:
The raw token is returned only to an active admin of this path. Legacy
hash-only links have no recoverable token and return null.

expiresInHours.description: How long the link stays usable. Null means no expiry.

token.description:
The raw share token, returned when an admin creates an invite and when an
active admin lists an encrypted reusable invite.

The database stores both a lookup hash and an encrypted copy. The latter
can be recovered only by an active admin; it is never public.

expiresAt.description: Expiry time. New invitations default to seven days; older links may lack one.

sehajPathId.description: Internal group id used to open the exact path after joining.

memberCount.description: How many people are already reading it.

membership.description: Whether the caller is already an active member of this path.

name.description:
Limited information about the path a link points at.

Deliberately not the path's reading position, member list or internal id:
holding a link is not membership, and this response is shown to somebody
who has not joined yet.

status.description:
A slot nobody used ends `SCHEDULED` with its time in the past — there is
no `MISSED`.

sehajPathId.description: The path this turn belongs to.

readerMemberId.description:
Who reads. Null is an OPEN slot — a time the group set aside without
deciding who takes it, claimable by any active member.

readerLabel.description:
Kept beside the id so the plan still reads correctly after a member
deletes their account.

createdByMemberId.description:
Who booked it. Differs from `readerMemberId` when an admin assigned the
time to somebody else.

startsAt.description: UTC. Display and reminders use the member's timezone; this does not.

isMine.description: True when the caller is the reader.

assignedByOther.description:
True when this is the caller's turn but somebody else booked it, so the
plan can say "Assigned by Amrit" rather than presenting it as their choice.

stateVersion.description:
Bumped by every group change. Compare it against the last one seen to
decide whether the slots below are worth re-rendering.

readerMemberId.description:
Who reads.

Omit to book for yourself. An admin may pass another active member's id to
assign the time to them, or `null` to leave the slot open for anybody to
claim. A non-admin passing anything but their own id is refused.

endsAt.description: End of the turn, UTC. Must be after `startsAt`.

startsAt.description: New start time. Omit to keep the stored one.

endsAt.description: New end time. Omit to keep the stored one.

slotEndsAt.description:
When this turn's reading time ends, or null when it holds no slot.

Sent as booking context for calendar/history displays. It is not a hard
session deadline: a connected reader may continue after this time until
they finish or an eligible booked reader explicitly takes over.

status.description: Only one session per path may be `LIVE` — the database enforces it.

endReason.description: Why the reading stopped. Null while live and for historical legacy rows.

startAng.description: Where the path stood when this turn began.

currentAng.description: Where the reader has reached. While LIVE, this is what followers render.

slotId.description:
The slot this turn was taken under. Null when the reading began with no
slot booked, or when the slot was later removed.

verseId.description: The verse the member has read to.

scrollPosition.description: Scroll offset within the ang, so a reader returns to the exact line rather than the top of the page.

applied.description: Whether this save moved the group position. False when the group had already read past this point — the position is never moved backwards.

expectedStartAng.description:
Where the client believed this turn began.

Compared against the session's recorded start. If they differ the path has
moved since — another device finished first, or this is a stale retry — and
the write is refused rather than rewinding the whole group.

Client-generated path id (uuid). Supply this so the app can create the
path locally and use it instantly, then sync whenever the network allows —
retries with the same id are idempotent (no duplicate paths). Omit to let
the server mint one.

Days the path was read (ISO "YYYY-MM-DD"). Merged by union with the
server's set — reading days are monotonic and are never removed, so a
device that is behind cannot wipe days recorded elsewhere.

baseUpdatedAt.description:
The `updatedAt` the client last saw for this path (ms since epoch). When
provided, the update is rejected with 409 if the server row is newer —
optimistic concurrency for multi-device edits.

settings.description:
The user's Sehaj Path preferences, returned verbatim as they were saved.
Keys are app-owned (see UpsertSehajPathSettingsDto); the server does not
interpret them.

The user's Sehaj Path preferences, stored verbatim. Keys are owned by the
app so new toggles can ship without a backend change — the server never
interprets these values, it only persists and echoes them. The known keys
today are `fontSize`, `larivaar`, `paragraphMode`, `vishraam`,
`vishraamsSource`, `angsFormat` and `consent`, but any JSON object is
accepted. Overall request size is bounded by the global body-parser limit.

When this device last synced (ms since epoch); 0/absent on first sync.

settings.description:
The device's current settings snapshot (opaque). When present it is applied
and stamped with the SERVER clock — last write to the server wins (no
device clocks involved). Include it only when settings changed locally
since the last sync; omit it otherwise so a stale device cannot overwrite
newer settings from another device.

paths.description:
The authoritative set of the user's live (non-deleted) paths after the
merge. The client should replace its local set with these.

settings.description:
The authoritative settings document after the last-write-wins merge, or
null if the user has none.

syncedAt.description:
Server time of this sync (ms since epoch). Store it verbatim and send it
as `lastSyncedAt` on the next sync — never use the device clock, which may
be skewed against the server's tombstone/merge timestamps.

deletedPathIds.description:
Ids of paths that are deleted server-side (tombstoned by this or another
device). The client should remove these locally.

appLink.description:
The app's own URL scheme, without "://". Opens the installed app on both
platforms and is the route that needs nothing compiled into Sundar Gutka:
an implicit VIEW intent is exempt from Android package visibility, so a
scheme set here reaches a newly added app with no manifest entry and no
app release. iOS still needs the scheme listed in
LSApplicationQueriesSchemes, which is why androidPkg and this both exist.
